subject: Commit amendment: expanded GPU allocation and throughput SLOs for model mix change
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@shoplane.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: sarah@avacloud.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FYI — renewal approaching; need larger GPUs + reranker add-on

Jonas,

Our renewal is up in December and the product team has validated the plan to move two workloads to a 70k-context LLM (longer context) and to enable a reranker pipeline for several flows. That change means our per-hour token throughput and KV cache behavior will shift. We ran an internal perf run last week and the ops team is forecasting ~2.4x peak GPU usage on current dedicated pools.

Can Redwood help sketch what a committed amendment would look like? We want reserved capacity (predictable throughput) and a throughput SLO during peak windows. Also need an estimate for incremental monthly commit and price guidance, and any term changes if we extend to 24 months.

Attachments: internal perf summary (attached to this thread).

Thanks — Tom
Product Ops, ShopLane
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@shoplane.com>
Cc: sarah@avacloud.com, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FYI — renewal approaching; need larger GPUs + reranker add-on

Tom — thanks for the clear heads-up. High level response below so your procurement team has something to react to quickly; I'll follow up with a formal amendment and capacity worksheet.

Summary of approach:
- Dedicated reserved pool sizing: we recommend adding a +16 A100-equivalent GPU buffer (can be split into two reserved pools for routing isolation) to cover the 70k-context model and reranker peak.
- Throughput guarantee: we can provide a peak-window throughput SLO (p95 tail during 8am–8pm local) with automatic overflow to burst capacity; SLO pricing has a premium of ~12% on top of committed GPU units.
- Term and pricing: 12-month vs 24-month tradeoff: 24-month commitment reduces unit price by ~7% and gives priority burst credits.
- Migration considerations: prefix/KV cache priming, model quantization recommendations, and an initial 2-week canary with metrics checks.

I'll loop in Marcus for an ops-level sizing worksheet and Monica for procurement/terms. If you can share the internal perf doc and expected qps distribution by hour that helps tighten the numbers.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FYI — renewal approaching; need larger GPUs + reranker add-on

Jonas / team — I reviewed ShopLane's perf artifact. Quick notes:

- Model mix: primary LLM is a 70k-context, 16B+ family (we saw the memory and KV pressure in their run). Reranker runs are short but high-concurrency and benefit from CPU+GPU batching.
- Sizing: baseline reserved pool increase of +12 A100-eq for the LLM and +4 A100-eq designated for reranker concurrency is reasonable. If they want a single pool for simplicity, add +18 to keep headroom for eviction and caching churn.
- Autoscaling & burst: Recommend committed pool + a burst slab (uncommitted) sized to handle 1.5x their observed peak for 3 hours/day. This reduces the upfront commit while meeting peak SLOs.
- Ops notes: need to enable optimized KV caching (prefix shards) and apply quantization profile 'q4_512' on the 70k variant to improve throughput without major quality loss.

I'm attaching a capacity_planner_v3.xlsx with two scenarios (split pools vs single pool) and estimated monthly commit delta.

- Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_planner_v3.xlsx
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FYI — renewal approaching; need larger GPUs + reranker add-on

Team — drafting the commercial amendment now. Key commercial items to confirm with ShopLane:

1) Committed units: either +12L (LLM) +4R (reranker) or single +18 pool. Need their sign-off on choice.
2) Term: offer 24-month with 7% discount vs 12-month baseline.
3) Throughput SLO: p95 trailing latency for peak window with a 12% SLO premium. Include 3 allowed SLO misses per year before remediation credits.
4) Priority burst credits: for 24-month deal include 200 burst GPU-hours/month.
5) Billing: monthly invoice against committed GPU-hours, overage billed at on-demand rate.

I'll prepare a redline (amendment_redlines.pdf) and include DocuSign link. Jonas — can you confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether ShopLane's procurement requires a PO upfront?

Best,
Monica Patel
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: commit_amendment_draft.docx, amendment_redlines.pdf
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@shoplane.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FYI — renewal approaching; need larger GPUs + reranker add-on

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement prefers monthly invoices and will issue a PO once we agree on the final committed unit counts and term. ShopLane favors the split-pool approach to limit noisy neighbor effects. We are inclined to take 24-month with the 7% discount and the burst credits. A couple of asks before we sign:

- Can Redwood include an appendix that documents the quantization profile and any expected model quality delta for the 70k-context variant? We need that for our ML QA sign-off.
- During the initial 2-week canary, can Redwood provide daily latency and token-cost reports via shared Drive link and one dedicated onboarding Slack channel?

If you send the DocuSign with the split-pool numbers (+12L +4R), 24 months, monthly billing, and the SLO appendix, I can get PO in the next 5 business days.

Tom Hayes
Product Ops, ShopLane
